parsed.explanation: The division is comparatively restrained—no state bathroom ban, vetoed anti-trans bills, employment protections and municipal accommodation ordinances—and a July 2026 assessment places it in the low-risk group for targeting trans adults. But the national framework governs the traveller-facing border and custody: passport/visa sex-marker restrictions, refusal where documents are discrepant, possible fraud/lifetime-ineligibility findings, federal facility exclusion by birth sex, and documented abuse in immigration custody. These are universal or high-severity exposures with no demonstrated working remedy for visitors. Local negatives—no gender-identity hate-crime coverage, an available panic defence, Pride collapse, youth-targeting laws—add friction but no documented visitor violence. The division sits below the 0.45 anchors because the national document/facility regime is sharper and less remedied, but above severe risk because trans identity is not criminalised and local adult-targeting restraint is documented.
